The first edition came out in 1951, but under two titles. The UK edition, published by Victor Gollancz, was titled Speak, Memory. It was first published in a single volume in 1951 as Speak, Memory in the United Kingdom and as Conclusive Evidence in the United States. A bookseller listing names the US publisher as Harper & Brothers, New York. This is an augmented revised edition of a book that was originally published by Harper & Brothers, New York in 1951 under the title of 'Conclusive Evidence'. A Kirkus listing gives the 1951 publisher as Putnam, which conflicts with the Harper attribution, so I'd treat that as unsettled.

The title Speak, Memory was used for the later editions. A revised Russian version followed in 1954, called Drugie berega (Other Shores). The revised English edition appeared in 1966 as Speak, Memory: An Autobiography Revisited, published by G.P. Putnam's Sons, New York.
